calibrations.pageSubtitle: Bias, dark and flat frames from your telescopes, grouped by exposure, binning, gain and temperature.

typeDescription.bias: Zero-length exposures that capture the sensor's fixed read noise, used to remove it from every other calibration frame.
typeDescription.dark: Exposures taken with the sensor covered, matched to a light frame's exposure, gain, and temperature, used to subtract thermal noise.
typeDescription.flat: Evenly-illuminated exposures used to correct vignetting and dust motes across the frame.
typeDescription.flatDark: Dark frames matched to a flat's (usually much shorter) exposure, used when flats aren't bias-corrected instead.
typeDescription.mixed: Calibration frames archived as your Dwarf telescope wrote them, a blend of frame types the device does not separate.

calibrations.empty: Nothing archived yet. Bias, dark, flat and flat-dark folders are picked up automatically the next time a telescope syncs or a folder import runs.

fitsViewer.locationAccessDenied: Location access was denied. Set your location in Settings instead.
fitsViewer.locationUnavailable: Could not get your location. Set it in Settings instead.
fitsViewer.nearMissExplanation: No cataloged satellite was confirmed inside the FOV during this exposure. These satellites passed nearby and may be the source - TLE accuracy degrades over time, so a close pass could still be a match. The trail may also be classified debris or an uncataloged object.
fitsViewer.noCatalogedSatellites: No cataloged satellites found passing this FOV during the exposure.
fitsViewer.locationNeededBody: This frame doesn't include observer coordinates, and no location is saved in Settings. Share your location to identify which satellite made this trail.
fitsViewer.step1Body: The FITS image is scanned for straight bright streaks using projection analysis across 180 angles. Background gradients and nebulosity are subtracted first, and stars are masked so only linear features remain as candidates.
fitsViewer.step2Body: If a trail is found, the FITS header is read for the exposure start time and sky coordinates (RA/Dec). Those are used to query an orbital catalog (TLE data) and compute which satellites were crossing that patch of sky during the exposure window.
fitsViewer.aboutResultsBody: Satellites confirmed inside the field of view during the exposure are listed first. When no exact match is found, nearby candidates are shown — TLE orbital data degrades over time, so a satellite that passed close to the edge may still be the source. The trail could also be uncataloged debris.
